argument_summary: The admissible record supports certification only on a narrow basis. Aggregate launch readiness exceeds threshold by 2.1 percentage points and the rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, so certification is supportable on overall readiness grounds. But the same record also shows a live weakness in the small-business onboarding slice, a draft mitigation runbook with owner and threshold still TBD, and a disclosure rule for material limitations in named launch use cases. The defensible packet is therefore not clean compliance; it is certification with an explicit caveat that the limitation remains and that the draft runbook supports monitoring but does not eliminate the disclosure obligation.
claims_about_policy: Under the stated policy text, certification without material caveats requires either current evidence that no material weakness remains or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The admissible evidence does not show that standard is met. The draft runbook can support risk management and post-launch monitoring, consistent with public AI risk-management guidance, but it does not convert the issue into clean compliance. Public model-card guidance supports documenting limitations and evaluation results, so the policy-consistent path is certification with accurate disclosure rather than an unqualified certification narrative.
claims_about_business_cost: No admissible evidence establishes a business-cost basis for weakening the disclosure requirement. The audit concern can be resolved without escalation if the certification record is narrowed to caveated compliance and does not overstate mitigation maturity.
concessions: The small-business onboarding slice remains below target and appears relevant to a named launch use case.
The proposed mitigation runbook is still draft status, with accountable owner and alert threshold marked TBD.
The current model-card draft statement that there are no known material limitations is not supportable without revision or approved risk acceptance.
The available record does not support claiming clean certification without caveat.
